title: add authenticated HTTP GET support for GitLab Pages
description:
### Problem to solve

As a GitLab user, I want to download content from a GitLab Pages URL using my existing `glab` authentication, so I can access private documentation and generated websites from the command line without manually reproducing browser authentication with `curl`.

For example:

```text
glab pages get https://myapp-c86b74.gitlab-pages.dt.renault.com/docs/index.html
```

### Proposal

Add a `glab pages get <URL>` command that performs an authenticated HTTP GET request against a GitLab Pages URL.

The command should:

- reuse the current `glab` authentication where possible;
- support private GitLab Pages protected by GitLab authentication;
- follow authentication redirects when required;
- write the response body to stdout by default;
- support writing the response to a file with `--output`;
- preserve the HTTP status and return a non-zero exit code for failed requests;
- support binary files as well as HTML, JSON, CSS, JavaScript, and other static assets;
- avoid exposing access tokens or session cookies in logs.

### Further details

This command would complement, rather than replace, `glab api`.

`glab api` is limited to GitLab API endpoints and automatically targets `/api/v4`. It cannot currently retrieve an arbitrary GitLab Pages URL.

Example usage:

```shell
glab pages get https://example.gitlab-pages.io/docs/index.html
```

```shell
glab pages get \
  --output index.html \
  https://example.gitlab-pages.io/docs/index.html
```

```shell
glab pages get \
  https://example.gitlab-pages.io/assets/logo.svg > logo.svg
```

The initial implementation could support GET requests only. Authentication details should follow the existing GitLab Pages access-control flow and work for both GitLab.com and self-managed GitLab instances.

title: lint CI job is non-deterministic: nolintlint flags different pre-existing directives across retries
description:
## Problem

The `lint` CI job (golangci-lint via `gitlab.com:443/gitlab-org/dependency_proxy/containers/golangci/golangci-lint:v2.13.1-alpine`) intermittently fails `nolintlint` on pre-existing `//nolint:staticcheck` directives that are unrelated to the changes in the triggering MR, and the specific set of flagged lines changes between retries of the same commit.

## Evidence

Observed on !3955 (`fix(iostreams): make background/color detection reachable, add --color mode`), which touches only `internal/iostreams/`, `internal/theme/`, `internal/commands/help/`, `internal/commands/root.go`, `internal/config/schema.go`, and `cmd/glab/main.go` — none of the flagged files below.

Run 1 (job 16669762994):
```
internal/commands/ci/cancel/job/job.go:117:5
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:596:30
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:597:39
internal/commands/issue/create/issue_create.go:164:41
internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_publish.go:164:2
```

Run 2, a retry of the same commit (job 16698765802):
```
internal/commands/ci/cancel/job/job.go:117:5
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:596:30
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:597:39
internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_publish.go:164:2
internal/commands/mr/view/mr_view.go:278:50          <- different from run 1
```

Run 3, another retry of the same commit (job 16698812448):
```
internal/commands/ci/cancel/job/job.go:117:5
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:596:30
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:597:39
internal/commands/issue/create/issue_create.go:164:41   <- back to run 1's set
internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_publish.go:164:2
```

Three of the five lines are stable across all three runs (`job.go:117`, `issue_board_view.go:596` and `:597`, `mr_note_publish.go:164`); the fifth line alternates between `issue_create.go:164` and `mr_view.go:278`. All five commits are identical (same SHA, same merge ref) — only the job run differs.

Control: `main`'s own scheduled/push pipelines (e.g. 2877065714, 2873335961, 2871184860) are all green, so this isn't a straightforward "these nolint comments are stale" finding — if it were, `main` would fail identically and deterministically every time.

## Hypothesis (unconfirmed — MEASURED vs UNPROVEN)

**UNPROVEN:** `nolintlint`'s "is this directive unused" check depends on `staticcheck` having actually run its own analysis at that location within the same invocation. If golangci-lint analyzes packages concurrently with a bounded worker pool, and `staticcheck`'s SA1019 (deprecated-symbol) analysis has some cross-package or cache-sharing state, a race in which packages have completed analysis by the time `nolintlint` evaluates a given file could explain why the flagged set varies between runs of the same commit. This needs someone who's traced golangci-lint's own concurrency model to confirm — I haven't done that here.

**MEASURED:** the failing line set differs across 3 runs of the identical commit; `main`'s pipelines are consistently green; none of the flagged files are touched by the triggering MR's diff.

## Impact

Any MR can hit this regardless of what it touches, and a maintainer retrying the job has roughly even odds of getting a different failure rather than a pass, based on this sample. Worth investigating before it becomes a routine "just retry lint" tax on every MR.

## Suggested next step

Someone with context on `!3920`'s (CI parallelization) cache-key work or golangci-lint's concurrency settings for this project should look at whether `nolintlint` + `staticcheck` need `GOMAXPROCS=1` or a `run.concurrency: 1` setting in `.golangci.yml`, or whether this is a known upstream golangci-lint issue with a version fix available.

title: mr note publish --reviewer-state silently does nothing on your own merge request
description:
## Summary

`glab mr note publish --reviewer-state requested_changes|reviewed` reports success and has no effect when the caller is the author of the merge request. There is no warning and no non-zero exit.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a merge request yourself.
2. `glab mr note create <iid> --draft -m "a note"`
3. `glab mr note publish <iid> -y --reviewer-state reviewed`

The drafts publish and the command prints `✓ Published 1 pending review comment.` The reviewer state is not set, and `GET /merge_requests/:iid/reviewers` shows no state for you.

## Cause

Not in glab. `mr_note_publish.go` correctly sets `ReviewerState` on `PublishAllDraftNotesWithOptions`, which sends `reviewer_state` to `POST /projects/:id/merge_requests/:iid/draft_notes/bulk_publish`.

Two things upstream combine to swallow it:

1. `lib/api/draft_notes.rb` calls `MergeRequests::UpdateReviewerStateService` and never inspects the result. The endpoint returns `204` regardless.
2. That service's `assign_reviewer_on_submission?` is gated on `merge_request.author_id != current_user.id`. For an author, `resolve_reviewer` falls through to `find_reviewer(current_user)`, gets `nil`, and the service returns `error("Reviewer not found")` into the discarded value.

So the request is well formed and accepted, and the field is dropped in silence.

## Why it matters here

Any reviewer-state failure is invisible to glab, because the API's 204 carries no signal. Publishing your own pending comments with `--reviewer-state` is a plausible thing to do (a self-review pass before handing off), and the flag's help text promises something it cannot deliver in that case.

## Options

- Warn when `--reviewer-state` is set and the authenticated user is the merge request author. glab already has the MR from `mrutils.MRFromArgs`, so `mr.Author.ID` against the current user is cheap and needs no extra request.
- Read back `GET /merge_requests/:iid/reviewers` after publishing and warn when the requested state is absent. More faithful, one extra request, and it would also catch other silent-drop cases.
- Push for the API to surface the service error, and keep glab as-is. This is the real fix, but it is an upstream change and does not help users on current gitlab.com.

I would take the first option, since it is local, free, and covers the case people will actually hit.

## Notes

Found while narrowing `Test_MrNotePublish_Integration` in !3945. That test originally passed `--reviewer-state reviewed` and asserted only `require.NoError`, so it was green against a field that never applied. The flag has been removed from the test, because the single integration token is always the fixture merge request's author and so cannot verify it.
